You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 57f71c974d750b0b46e44118a11011aa70f3c66c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Steve Stagg <stestagg@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Apr 2014 13:36:53 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Fix some bugs introduced in
 c57baae4775f4e665b7e158582234ac558a2bf7b preventing the 'mime' routing
 function from working with request variables, and actually return the found
 mimetype

The uwsgi_route_var_mime function had two errors preventing it from (afaics ever) working:
 1. Redefine the 'ret' variable inside an if block. This meant that if the uwsgi_get_mime_type function ever actually found a matching mimetype, the length of the matching value would be corectly set, but the function returns NULL (the value of the function-level ret variable)
 2. The function was looking up the request variable correctly, BUT then passing in the raw config string to uwsgi_get_mime_type NOT the resolved varible value, making the lookup just a waste of cycles.
---
 core/routing.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/core/routing.c b/core/routing.c
index f42ecd26..bc421855 100644
--- a/core/routing.c
+++ b/core/routing.c
@@ -1704,7 +1704,7 @@ static char *uwsgi_route_var_mime(struct wsgi_request *wsgi_req, char *key, uint
         char *var_value = uwsgi_get_var(wsgi_req, key, keylen, &var_vallen);
         if (var_value) {
 		size_t mime_type_len = 0;
-		char *ret = uwsgi_get_mime_type(key, keylen, &mime_type_len);
+		ret = uwsgi_get_mime_type(var_value, var_vallen, &mime_type_len);
 		if (ret) *vallen = mime_type_len;
         }
         return ret;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by two main issues in the `uwsgi_route_var_mime` function. First, the `ret` variable was redefined inside an if block, which led to the function returning NULL instead of the correct MIME type when a match was found. Second, the function was incorrectly passing the raw configuration string to `uwsgi_get_mime_type` instead of the resolved variable value, resulting in ineffective lookups and wasted processing cycles.
